title: Commons Text CSV field quoting across a Commons Lang upgrade
summary: Check the characters returned by the original StringEscapeUtils.escapeCsv on both sides of Apache Commons Text PR #586.

change.description: PR #586 changes the production dependency org.apache.commons:commons-lang3 from 3.16.0 to 3.17.0.

verdictLabel: 156/156 fields preserved on each JVM classpath; native workflow stopped at class-file intake
notes: This published calibration is excluded from both evaluation cohorts. The full-source JVM run compiles both pinned Commons Text trees. The target workflow compiles the original entry and translator classes from the same revisions. Each replay invokes the public method.

The old and new full client JARs are byte-identical. All 34 original StringEscapeUtilsTest tests passed on both JVM classpaths. The quote-doubling omission disagreed on 71 inputs, including a single double quote, and failed both original CSV escaping tests.

The standard route stopped before checker launch while decoding a modified UTF-8 NUL in the original StringEscapeUtils constant pool. A separate direct CLI probe on the full production classes refused before.org.apache.commons.text.StringEscapeUtils.<clinit>() under strict gaps.

On the complete Linux JDK 21 Maven CI lane, both revisions reported 1305 tests and all 34 StringEscapeUtils tests passed. With ordinary local hostname resolution, the two errors remaining on each side require the external Apache DNS or HTTPS endpoint.
